title: The human knot: untangle without letting go
description: Everyone holds two strangers' hands across a circle, and the group becomes a single tangled knot. The only way out is talking, ducking, stepping over and laughing — together, without anyone letting go.

body.heading: Tie the knot
paragraphs: Stand in a close circle, shoulder to shoulder — six to twelve people is ideal. Everyone reaches both hands into the middle and takes hold of two different people's hands, not the hands of anyone standing directly beside them. What you have made is the human knot: a single tangled loop of arms and people.

The task is simple to say and gloriously awkward to do: untangle yourselves back into an open circle without anyone letting go of either hand. Hands may swivel in each other's grip so wrists stay comfortable, but the chain must never break.

body.heading: Untangling is a conversation
paragraphs: There is no strength move that solves a human knot. The groups that succeed talk constantly: someone ducks under an arm here, two people step over joined hands there, the whole circle shuffles a quarter-turn at someone's suggestion. Every tangle has slack somewhere — finding it is a team sport in itself.

If you reach a true deadlock after ten minutes, allow one handhold to be re-gripped — unclasp and rejoin the same two hands from the other side — and count it as a team decision, not a failure. Finish in a circle, hands still joined, and take the bow together.

takeaway: Grab two hands across the circle, then talk, duck and step your way back to an open ring — the knot only unties if the whole group thinks together.
materials: A clear, flat space with room to shuffle and duck
Comfortable clothes you can bend and step over arms in
supervision: An adult or group leader should play or referee for groups including children, watching that twists stay gentle and calling a pause if anyone's arm or shoulder is strained.
safetyNotes: Stop at once if anyone's shoulder, wrist or back hurts — re-grip a handhold rather than forcing a twist.
Take rings, watches and bracelets off before playing so joined hands cannot catch or scratch.
Move slowly on smooth floors; a whole circle shuffling at once can unbalance the steadiest player.
